questions.question: Explain two reasons why Britain followed a policy of appeasement. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: War weariness: the memory of WWI (750,000 British dead) made the public and politicians desperate to avoid another war. Military unpreparedness: Britain's armed forces were not ready for war in 1938 - the RAF needed expansion and the army was too small for continental warfare. Appeasement bought time for rearmament.

questions.question: How far was appeasement justified? (8 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Appeasement was partially justified in 1938: Britain was militarily unprepared; the RAF needed time to develop radar and Spitfires; public opinion strongly opposed war; and some German grievances (especially self-determination for Sudeten Germans) appeared legitimate. questions.correctAnswer: Appeasement was not cowardly - it was a rational policy based on genuine concerns: avoiding another catastrophic war, military unpreparedness, and the belief that some German grievances were legitimate. questions.question: Explain why appeasement was abandoned in March 1939. (8 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Appeasement was abandoned because Hitler's seizure of Czechoslovakia (15 March 1939) proved that his aims were conquest, not self-determination. He had broken his Munich promise that the Sudetenland was his "last territorial demand." The British public and Parliament now saw Hitler as an untrustworthy aggressor.
